name: Thoughts Are All Over the Place: On the Underthinking of o1-Like LLMs
authors: Yue Wang, Qiuzhi Liu, Jiahao Xu, Tian Liang, Xingyu Chen, Zhiwei He, Linfeng Song, Dian Yu, Juntao Li, Zhuosheng Zhang, Rui Wang, Zhaopeng Tu, Haitao Mi, Dong Yu et al.; lead affiliation Tencent AI Lab (with Soochow University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University)
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2501.18585, Jan 2025); subsequently accepted at NeurIPS 2025 (poster, title 'On the Underthinking of Long Reasoning Models'). Semantic Scholar indexes venue as arXiv.org.
reflection_type: calibration/probing (analysis of the model's own self-reflective thought-switching behavior); the proposed fix is a decoding-time intervention (Thought Switching Penalty, TIP) rather than a verbal self-critique loop. Reflection here is the o1-like model's native strategy-switching/reflective CoT, which the paper analyzes and constrains.
feedback_source: self-generated (the model's own long chain-of-thought is analyzed); ground-truth-oracle is used offline only for the analysis/metric (LLM-as-judge with DeepSeek-R1-Distill models assesses thought correctness, and known answers label correct/incorrect responses). The TIP intervention itself uses no external feedback at decode time.
iteration_structure: single-shot (TIP is a single-pass decoding modification; no iterative refine or retry). Analysis additionally combines TIP with best-of-N sampling (Self-Consistency, Laconic Decoding) for evaluation.
reflection_object: reasoning chain (the intermediate 'thoughts' / reasoning strategies within a single long CoT). TIP modifies the decoding distribution over thought-switching tokens to keep the model elaborating the current reasoning thought instead of prematurely switching to a new one; it does not modify weights, prompt, or stored skills.
reward_or_critic_model: none for the deployed TIP method (training-free decoding penalty). For the offline analysis only, an LLM-as-judge (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B) is used to assess whether each thought can lead to the correct answer (achieving 82.9% / 81.8% agreement accuracy on correct/incorrect examples).
distillation_target: none (no reflection artifact is distilled or persisted; TIP is an inference-time logit adjustment with no stored memory, skill, rule, prompt, or weight update).
emergent_vs_engineered: Analyzes RL-emergent reflective behavior (the native strategy-switching/reflection of RL-trained o1-like models such as QwQ-32B-Preview and DeepSeek-R1), and proposes an engineered decoding-time scaffold (TIP) to constrain that emergent behavior. So: emergent behavior studied, engineered fix applied (no fine-tuning).
error_localization_granularity: step-level (per reasoning 'thought' / strategy segment). Underthinking is localized to the thought index where a correct-but-abandoned thought occurs; the underthinking metric measures the token position of the first correct thought within an incorrect response.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task (the analysis and the TIP penalty operate within a single problem's reasoning trace; no experience is transferred across tasks). Hyperparameters (alpha=3, beta=600) are tuned on AIME2022/23 and applied unchanged to other test sets, but no per-task learning occurs.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: mid-trajectory-recovery (TIP intervenes in-flight during decoding to discourage premature thought switching and keep the model on a promising path before it abandons it); it is not retry-based avoidance or post-hoc revision.
task_domains: math; QA/reasoning (graduate-level science). Specifically competition math (MATH, AIME) and graduate-level multiple-choice science (GPQA).
benchmarks: MATH500 (esp. Level 5 / MATH500-Hard), GPQA Diamond (198 questions), AIME2024 (30 problems); AIME2022 and AIME2023 used as a development/tuning set (90 instances total for assessment).
headline_result: Identifies 'underthinking': on AIME2024, o1-like LLMs consume on average 225% more tokens in incorrect responses than in correct ones, due to 418% more frequent thought switching, without improved accuracy. The training-free TIP decoding penalty consistently improves QwQ-32B-Preview Pass@1 accuracy while lowering the underthinking (UT) score: AIME2024 41.7 -> 45.8 (UT 72.4 -> 68.2), MATH500-Hard/Level5 82.8 -> 84.3 (UT 71.1 -> 69.7), GPQA Diamond 57.1 -> 59.3 (UT 59.1 -> 56.5), with no model fine-tuning.
baselines: Vanilla (standard) decoding of QwQ-32B-Preview; prompt engineering (DeepSeek-R1 + Prompt) as an alternative intervention; best-of-N selection baselines Self-Consistency and Laconic Decoding (shortest-of-N), each evaluated with and without TIP; also descriptive comparison against conventional LLMs (Qwen-Math-72B, Llama3.3-70B) that do not show the underthinking length gap.
gains_vs_baseline: TIP over vanilla QwQ-32B-Preview (Pass@1, same alpha=3/beta=600 hyperparameters): +4.1 points on AIME2024 (41.7 -> 45.8), +1.5 on MATH500-Hard (82.8 -> 84.3), +2.2 on GPQA Diamond (57.1 -> 59.3). When combined with best-of-N: with Self-Consistency, QwQ Pass@4 AIME2024 rises 43.7 -> 51.4 (+7.7); with Laconic Decoding, R1-Distill-Qwen-32B Pass@8 AIME2024 rises 74.4 -> 78.0 (+3.6) and UT 8.7 -> 7.3. Prompt engineering gives only modest changes vs TIP. UT scores consistently decrease, indicating more thorough reasoning.
compute_cost_profile: TIP itself adds negligible cost: it is a single-pass decoding-time logit adjustment on thought-switching tokens (alpha penalty for beta positions from each thought start), no fine-tuning, no extra forward passes vs standard decoding. The underlying problem it targets is wasted compute: incorrect responses use ~225% more tokens (e.g., AIME2024 incorrect 16,108 vs correct 5,549 tokens for QwQ; 26.4 vs 7.0 thoughts). Best-of-N variants (Self-Consistency / Laconic with N=4/8/16) multiply inference cost by N as expected.
known_limitations: Requires logit access (TIP could not be applied to DeepSeek-R1-671B via API, which forbids logit modification), so it is limited to open-weight models. Thought-switching tokens are heuristically identified (e.g., 'alternatively'), relying on LLM segmentation (Llama-3.3-70B) that is imperfect. Hyperparameters (alpha, beta) are tuned on AIME2022/23 and may need re-tuning. Gains on easier benchmarks (MATH500-Hard, GPQA) are modest (~1.5-2.2 points). The thought-correctness assessment uses LLM-as-judge (~82% agreement), introducing noise. The work analyzes only two/three open o1-like models on math/science.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: intrinsic-only for the deployed TIP method (training-free, no labels at decode time). For the offline diagnostic analysis and the underthinking metric, oracle-label/ground-truth (known correct answers) plus an LLM-judge are used to identify correct-but-abandoned thoughts; this oracle is only used to characterize the phenomenon, not by TIP at inference.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive (task-dependent magnitude). TIP improves accuracy across all three challenging test sets without label leakage at inference and reduces underthinking scores; gains are largest on the hardest set (AIME2024, +4.1) and modest elsewhere. The paper frames the issue as the o1-like models' native reflective thought-switching being net-negative when excessive; TIP corrects this by penalizing premature switching.
calibration_effect: not-measured (no explicit confidence-calibration / ECE analysis). The paper instead measures token-efficiency (the underthinking UT score) and accuracy. It documents that more capable models (DeepSeek-R1-671B) can paradoxically have higher UT scores on some sets, i.e. more elaborate but inefficient reasoning when uncertain.
failure_attribution_capability: classifies-failure-mode (taxonomy): formally defines and characterizes 'underthinking' as a distinct failure mode (premature abandonment of promising reasoning paths via excessive thought switching), distinguishing it from 'overthinking' (Chen et al. 2024) and from genuine lack of understanding; attributes failing steps via the first-correct-thought index and quantifies it with the UT metric.
failure_mode_addressed: underthinking: frequent thought-switching without sufficiently deep exploration of promising reasoning paths, leading to inadequate reasoning depth, wasted tokens, and lower accuracy on hard problems. Explicitly contrasted with overthinking. Maps to MAST-style reasoning failures such as superficial/inefficient self-reflection and premature termination of a line of reasoning (the paper also cites 'I give up' mid-reasoning as a form of underthinking).
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new dataset/benchmark; introduces a reusable metric (the underthinking score xi_UT measuring token efficiency in incorrect responses) and releases code at https://github.com/wangyuenlp/underthinking. Uses existing benchmarks (MATH500, GPQA Diamond, AIME).
builds_on: Overthinking analysis of o1-like LLMs (Chen et al. 2024, 'Do Not Think That Much for 2+3=?', arXiv:2412.21187) as a direct companion/counterpart; o1 and its replicas QwQ (Qwen 2024), DeepSeek-R1 (DeepSeek 2025), Kimi-1.5 (Kimi 2025); coverage/length penalties in neural machine translation (Tu et al. 2016; Wu et al. 2016) that inspire TIP; Self-Consistency (Wang et al. 2023) and Chain-of-Thought (Wei et al. 2022); Laconic Decoding (Raoof & Dimakis).
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited by subsequent efficient-reasoning / reasoning-length-control and reasoning-failure-analysis work, e.g. 'When More is Less: Understanding Chain-of-Thought Length in LLMs' (Wu et al. 2025), s1: Simple Test-Time Scaling (Muennighoff et al. 2025), 'Training Language Models to Reason Efficiently' (Arora & Zanette 2025); and later 2025-2026 works such as PathCal (state-aware reflection-marker calibration for efficient reasoning), STOP (structured on-policy pruning of long-form reasoning), TRIAGE (metacognitive control under resource constraints), EntroCut (entropy-guided adaptive CoT truncation), and surveys on mechanistic understanding of large reasoning models and their failures.
reasoning_model_native: true. The paper specifically targets o1/R1-style reasoning models with built-in long-CoT reflection (QwQ-32B-Preview, DeepSeek-R1-671B, DeepSeek-R1-Preview, R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, R1-Distill-Llama-70B); the underthinking phenomenon and the TIP fix are defined relative to their native thought-switching/reflective behavior, and explicitly do NOT manifest the same way in conventional LLMs (Qwen-Math-72B, Llama3.3-70B).
on_policy_distillation_link: Weak/indirect. TIP is a training-free, on-policy decoding-time steering of the model's own generation (no distillation, no weight update). It relates to on-policy distillation only insofar as it shapes on-policy reasoning trajectories at inference; some citing works (e.g. Self-Verified Distillation, STOP on-policy pruning) build on the underthinking lens within distillation/RL pipelines, but this paper itself performs no distillation.
sample_efficiency: TIP is applied with a single set of hyperparameters (alpha=3, beta=600) tuned via grid search over alpha in {3,5,10,20,30} and beta in {300,400,500,600,700} on the AIME2022/23 development set, then transferred unchanged. Pass@1 results are reported over 4 samples. Best-of-N analyses average over 10,000 random-sampling trials drawn from 32 generated responses per setting.
